newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate falls again, baht weaker late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate falls again, baht weaker late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate continued to fall to 7.00-8.00 percent in late trade on Thursday from 8.75-9.25 percent earlier amid steadily rising liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said most banks were still on the offer side today following a call this week by the central bank to commercial banks to cut local interest rates to help boost the economy.
"People expect a fall in local interest rates and higher liquidity after the central bank's request. So banks continue to offer funds for lending today," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond on Tuesday repeated a call for local banks to cut interest rates to help boost the sagging economy.
Several major local banks also recently announced plans to reduce their lending rates.
The lower dollar/baht swap premiums also encouraged the import of cheap foreign funds, dealers said.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium declined to 7.00/7.50 satangs per dollar late from 7.75/8.25 early.
The baht weakened further to 25.527-25.532 to the dollar late from 25.497-25.510 early on the dollar's strength abroad and high liquidity, dealers said.
The dollar/baht mid-rate was fixed at 25.49 against 25.48 on Wednesday.
